clue.text: Fish served for starters with beer and stuff?

parts.note: cod is a familiar sea fish

indicators.note: for starters asks for only the opening letter of the word served

parts.note: wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A pub order: fish with a pint, and all that sort of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes only S, the first letter of 'served'. WALLOP is British slang for beer, and 'stuff', as in 'stuff and nonsense', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the sense of rubbish talk is nonsense, the same meaning as this British slang word.

clue.text: Clown given fruit from palm tree

explanation.surface: A circus clown is handed a coconut.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous British circus performer, so the name stands for a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco was a celebrated circus clown's name, and coco is also the coconut, the nut borne by the coconut palm.

clue.text: Mostly impenetrable lairs

indicators.note: mostly means the word for impenetrable loses its final letter

parts.note: dense undergrowth or fog is impenetrable

explanation.surface: Animal hideouts that are, for the most part, impossible to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter E from DENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairs are the hideouts of wild animals, a synonym for their burrows and caves.

clue.text: Operation overseen by doctor, one in GP unit wildly celebrating

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece overseen by another sits below it

parts.note: Doctor Who is the television time traveller, so doctor gives his name

indicators.note: in places the one inside the letters of GP unit
wildly means the letters of one in GP unit are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A hospital report: a doctor supervises surgery while someone at the practice goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the television time traveller; 'overseen by' works because in a down clue the doctor sits above the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Whooping it up is an idiom for partying noisily, a lively form of having fun.

clue.text: Foreign statesman's number up after Liberal's taken over

indicators.note: after places the reversed number behind the Liberal letter
in a down clue up means the number is written bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A politician abroad finds his time is up once the Liberals take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works in a down clue, where the number reads bottom to top; 'taken over' just completes the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik leader of the 1917 Russian Revolution was a Russian statesman, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Society writer appears in public, exhausted

indicators.note: appears in places the society and writer letters inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A society columnist turns up at a public event, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author, but it is the humble pen; 'appears in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is exhausted has all been used up, as a budget is when too much is spent.

clue.text: This mostly restricts a person from Bangkok

indicators.note: restricts means the shortened word closes in around a
mostly means the word this loses its final letter

explanation.surface: This rule limits what a man from Bangkok may do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims This to THI, and 'restricts' has it enclose A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, so a native of the city is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Swimmer wearing cover on head gets close up

parts.note: someone with a hood over the head is hooded
to seal is to close something up tightly

explanation.surface: A swimmer in a cap gets near the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close up' reads as 'come near' but is SEAL, to close up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of Arctic seal whose male inflates a hood on its head, and seals are marine swimmers.

clue.text: They're cared for by doctors wearing tie inside trousers

parts.note: to be in a garment is to be wearing it

indicators.note: inside puts the tie within the word for trousers

parts.note: in America pants are trousers

explanation.surface: A medic's dress code: a tie tucked into the trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is the American sense of pants; 'inside' is the container signal and 'wearing' is the IN of in-patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital patients who stay on the ward are looked after by medical staff.

clue.text: Damned bewildered

explanation.surface: Two adjectives for someone cursed and confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Confounded is a mild curse meaning damned, as in that dratted thing, and also means utterly puzzled.

clue.text: Wicker basket from the supermarket?

explanation.surface: A wicker basket picked up at the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British supermarket chain; a coop is also a wicker basket or cage for poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop can be a basket-like wicker cage for hens, and the Co-op is a cooperative grocery chain in Britain.

clue.text: Sequence of pictures journey on farm vehicle

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sequence of pictures journey on farm vehicle (5,7)': S-TRIP CART-ON gives TRIP, CART and ON but no clue word supplies the S and the second O of STRIPCARTOON; the clue looks cut short and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sequence of pictures journey on farm vehicle

clue.text: Rolling Stones' repute, quite appealing?

indicators.note: rolling means the letters of the band name and repute are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones' reputation is rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' looks like part of the band's name but is the anagram signal for STONES REPUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up one's street is to one's taste, an idiom for being right for you.

clue.text: Night spot put ban on certain records

indicators.note: in a down clue the ban placed on the records sits below them

parts.note: singles are records carrying one main track
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A nightclub puts a ban on certain records.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts BAR below SINGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A singles bar is a nightclub where unattached people go to meet, a venue for evening drinking.

clue.text: Inordinate quantities of dead Indian

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Inordinate quantities of dead Indian (10)': OVER (dead) and DOSA (an Indian food) give OVERDOSA but no clue word supplies GE; the clue looks cut short and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Being resourceful, I have to pursue one new opening

indicators.note: to pursue means the contracted I have follows the other pieces

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a vent is an opening that lets air out
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Showing initiative, I must chase a fresh opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the definition of an opportunity, but it is a vent; 'to pursue' sets the contraction at the end, ignoring its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventive means full of new ideas, the quality of being clever at finding solutions.

clue.text: Unwisely maintain ultimate in silence, still?

indicators.note: unwisely means the letters of maintain are put into a careless new order
ultimate in asks for the closing letter of silence

explanation.surface: It is foolish to keep up the final silence, isn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwisely' rearranges MAINTAIN, and 'ultimate in' adds E, the last letter of 'silence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate has no life or motion, so it is still in the sense of motionless.

clue.text: Topic for debate in a newspaper?

explanation.surface: A subject for argument in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter under discussion, and also one copy or edition of a periodical.

clue.text: Author's success starts to revive keen interest

parts.note: to make a go of something is to make a success of it

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of revive, keen and interest

explanation.surface: A writer's triumph sparks fresh enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes R, K and I from the next three words. Maxim Gorky, also spelt Gorki, was a Russian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorky was the Russian novelist and playwright, a celebrated writer.

clue.text: Classic wit displayed by sailor in part of house

parts.note: an attic is the room under the roof
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor shows off his learned humour up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic salt is refined wit, after the elegant humour of ancient Athens; 'Classic' points to the classical world.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic salt is refined, delicate humour, named after Athenian wit and so a classical form of repartee.

clue.text: Developing slowly, perhaps 4 down's no republican

indicators.note: no means the republican letter is dropped from the word for the statesman at 4 down

parts.note: the Bolshevik statesman at 4 down is an example of one who overthrew a regime by force

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader who renounces republicanism comes round gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 down statesman is a Bolshevik who overthrew a regime, and 'no' removes R, for republican, from that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Change by gradual development, as in Darwin's theory of species, is the sense here.

clue.text: Asian kingdom

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Asian kingdom (5)': only the definition survives, with no wordplay, so the clue looks cut short and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Spray odd parts of Main Street

indicators.note: odd parts of asks for the first and third letters of the word main

explanation.surface: Water is sprayed on parts of the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts of' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of 'Main', M and I, and ST is the abbreviation for Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a fine spray of droplets, as from an atomiser.

clue.text: Do well, though not having good start in school

indicators.note: not having means the following letter is removed from the phrase for doing well

parts.note: to get on is to do well and prosper

indicators.note: start asks for the opening letter of the word good

explanation.surface: A pupil does well despite a poor beginning at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' drops G, the 'start' of 'good', from GET ON. The answer is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English boarding school founded by Henry VI.

clue.text: Attend strike

explanation.surface: Be present at a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, BE AT means attend.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at an event is to attend it, and to beat someone is to hit them.

clue.text: Satirical writer is on top, excited after hit

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the word for hit

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard

indicators.note: excited means the letters of is on top are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A satirist on top form gets worked up after a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' is the anagram signal, and 'hit' gives the less familiar verb lam, to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a mocking satirical piece, so its author is a satirist.

clue.text: He made films — Oliver?

explanation.surface: Did Oliver make movies?
explanation.walkthrough: Carol Reed was a British film director, who made the musical film Oliver!; Oliver Reed was a British actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Reed directed films such as The Third Man, and Oliver Reed was an actor bearing the same surname.

clue.text: Duke takes up residence in dwelling tonight

indicators.note: takes up residence in says the answer lives inside the words dwelling tonight

explanation.surface: A duke moves into a house for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Wellington was the British general who beat Napoleon at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley was created first Duke of this title after his victories over Napoleon.
